subject: Helix Labs — post-call technical decision brief and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@helixlabs.ai>, Miguel Santos <m.santos@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-19T16:02:00Z
Subject: Helix post-call: technical notes + clarification on SLOs

Hi Claire / Miguel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the items we need to validate to move to a proposal: 

Key pain points and goals (as we understood them):
- Production recommendation quality varies by workload (multi-domain prompts) and you need repeatable A/B comparisons before switching models.
- Tight p95 latency targets for inference driving customer experience; want predictable p95 under peak for 512–1024 token outputs.
- On-prem requirement for PHI-sensitive flows (some requests will never leave Helix VPC).
- Cost predictability for billing internal product teams (monthly line-item for inference).

SLO / workload numbers you mentioned in the call:
- Target p95 generation latency: 180 ms for mean request size ~512 tokens, allowance to 250 ms for 1024 tokens (please confirm).
- Expected concurrent RPS (steady-state): 75–120 req/s across two regions; burst to ~300 req/s during ETL windows.
- Average output length: 420–600 tokens; 99th percentile can be ~1200 tokens.

Model requirements & variants:
- Primary model: open Llama-3 variant (70B quantized) for best mix of quality/cost.
- Fallback: smaller 13B quantized variant for cost-sensitive / burst handling.

Topology options we discussed (high level):
1) Hybrid: Redwood-hosted control plane + private inference layer inside Helix VPC (Redwood Private) for PHI workloads + Dedicated pools for public product traffic. Good for compliance and predictable throughput.
2) Fully Hosted with Private Endpoints: fastest time to market, but requires encrypted egress agreements for PHI (less preferred).
3) On-prem appliance: if Helix wants entirely air-gapped deployments for regulated customers.

Immediate asks / clarifications for our team to size a proposal: 
1) Confirm the p95 latency target for 512 vs 1024 tokens (your call said ~180ms/250ms — please confirm).
2) Which percentage of traffic is PHI-bound (must stay on-prem)? A ballpark split will help sizing.
3) Any existing latency budget for pre-processing (tokenization/embedding calls) we should account for?

Attached: quick perf snapshot from our lab running Llama-3-70B quantized on H100 and batch/kv-cache tradeoffs (helix_perf_snapshot.csv).

Next step: once you confirm the three items above, we’ll assemble an ops-ready topology recommendation (estimated GPU counts, autoscale policy, and cost bands) and a draft SLA for review. Can we target a short follow-up call next Wednesday (May 24) for the deep-dive?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

--
Redwood Inference — unified runtime for predictable LLM inference
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@helixlabs.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <m.santos@helixlabs.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-19T18:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Helix post-call: technical notes + clarification on SLOs

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the concise summary — that matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) Latency targets: we can confirm 180 ms p95 for ~512 tokens; 250 ms p95 for ~1024 tokens is acceptable. For planning, treat these as hard targets for customer-facing endpoints.

2) PHI split: roughly 35% of requests are PHI-bound today and must remain inside our VPC. That will scale up as we roll out to additional enterprise customers.

3) Pre-processing budget: ~30 ms median for tokenization + enrichment; please include this in your end-to-end latency calculations.

Additional notes: 
- We will need the ability to A/B two model variants with consistent traffic split and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 Type II is required; we may request an on-site audit later this year.

We’re available for a detailed architecture session next Wednesday 2028-05-24 at 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

Attaching the short internal compliance checklist we referenced (not an NDA).

Regards,
Claire
Claire Zhou | Head of Platform Engineering, Helix Labs
claire.zhou@helixlabs.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@helixlabs.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T01:12:00Z
Subject: Internal: Helix follow-up — topology recommendation draft + questions

Ben / Rishi —

Recap from Claire: p95 180ms (512t) / 250ms (1024t), preproc budget ~30ms, 35% PHI on-prem. Good time to sketch a recommended architecture and resource estimate. High-level proposal (for discussion on Wed):

Recommended hybrid topology (Primary):
- Redwood Private (VPC deployment) for PHI traffic routed to on-prem inference nodes inside Helix VPC.
  - Model runbook: Llama-3-70B quantized x4 replicas on H100 (sustained RPS budget), batching tuned to maintain 180ms p95 for 512 tokens.
  - KV cache colocated with inference nodes to reduce repeated prefix costs.
- Redwood Dedicated pool (hosted) for public traffic with automatic model-fallback to 13B for bursts.
- Smart routing policy: route PHI requests to VPC endpoints, non-PHI to Dedicated; overflow/burst policy to spill to 13B on Dedicated.

Sizing & perf assumptions (initial):
- Steady 100 req/s with avg 500 tokens => estimate 6 H100s in VPC for PHI slice (35% traffic).
- Hosted Dedicated for remaining traffic: 10 A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale to handle 300 req/s burst using 13B fallback.
- Batch sizes: dynamic batching target 4–8 in steady state to optimize throughput without violating p95.

Risk & open items for Wed:
- Confirm whether Helix can accept our Private control-plane (they said yes, but need contract confirmation).
- Verify whether GPU choice (H100 vs A100) is constrained by procurement/on-prem availability.
- SLA wording for model rollback time and failover expectations.

Action items I’ll own for Wed:
- Produce a one-page topology diagram + cost banding and GPU counts for the hybrid option.
- Pull quantized throughput runs for the Llama-3-70B on H100/A100 and attach (short CSV).

Ben/Rishi — can you each take one of the tech owners for the deep-dive? Ben you own the Dedicated/hosted routing and autoscale policy; Rishi you own the VPC/Private control-plane and KMS/HSM notes.

Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
